title: Rapid fallback enforcer and tenant-mute windowing hotpatch
author: Lena Morales
description: Context: During the 2026-02-12 regional cascading failover incident we observed large-scale KV-cache invalidations and aggressive fanout across healthy nodes when a noisy tenant caused transient latency spikes. The side effects were higher tail latency for unrelated tenants and prolonged failovers. Motivation: Introduce a lightweight rapid-fallback enforcer that applies a conservative, local fallback policy at the routing layer to avoid wholesale regional failovers and to give the control plane time to reconcile. Complement this with a tenant-mute window that temporarily reduces priority for noisy tenants rather than evicting them, enabling graceful degradation and faster recovery. Changes: 1) serving/runtime/fallback: add RapidFallbackEnforcer which intercepts decision points and enforces a fanout cap and soft-circuit cooldown; 2) controlplane/policies: add TenantMuteWindow and mute propagation with TTL and decay heuristics; 3) observability: new telemetry streams and alerts (fallback_telemetry) with derived SLO delta metrics; 4) tests: chaos and unit tests to validate behavior under induced latencies; 5) docs/ops: routing guidance and emergency rollback steps. Rollout plan: staged canary to 5% of traffic in us-west-1, monitor SLO deltas and fallback_telemetry for 30m, expand to 25% if no regressions, full rollout after 2x successful canaries. Backout: revert head branch or flip runtime flag. Checklist: - [x] Implementation for enforcer and tenant-mute - [x] Unit and integration tests - [x] Canary rollout plan documented - [x] Observability dashboards and alerts wired - [x] Linear and incident links added Related work: builds on prior tenant-prioritizer pieces (ENG-2105) and ties into ongoing SLO-driven routing design (ENG-3421).
